blocks.text: Faculty of Medicine of Algiers Dr REBAÏNE
To survive, the cell needs energy.
Aerobic metabolism, one of several ways of producing energy in the cell, depends on a stable supply of O₂ and nutrients from the environment coupled with the elimination of CO₂.
The supply of O2 to cells and the elimination of CO2 require the intervention of the ventilatory (alveolar hematosis) and cardiovascular (gas transport) systems.
Respiration is the set of phenomena which contribute to ensuring gas exchanges between the ambient environment and the living cell.

III-Non-hematotic functions of the respiratory system
Besides this gas exchange function, the respiratory system has other functions.
1-A purification function: the air is in fact loaded with inert or living particles.
Like all other epithelia that are in contact with the environment, the respiratory epithelium is well equipped: mechanisms trap and destroy dangerous substances before they can enter the body.
III-Non-hematotic functions of the respiratory system
The lung has a considerable endothelial surface area over which all cardiac output passes. It therefore has a privileged position for metabolizing circulating substances.
III-Non-hematotic functions of the respiratory system
-contains a fibrinolytic system which lyses clots in the pulmonary vessels;
- releases different substances which enter the systemic arterial blood (prostaglandins, histamine, etc.);
-extract from systemic venous blood other substances which reach it via the pulmonary artery (serotonin, norepinephrine, etc.);

-activates angiotensin I (inactive decapeptide) to angiotensin II; a vasopressor which stimulates the secretion of aldosterone, thanks to the converting enzyme located on the surface of the endothelial cells of the pulmonary capillaries;
III-Non-hematotic functions of the respiratory system
3-In terms of behavior: phonation, swallowing, hiccups, laughing, yawning, sniffing, sighing, vomiting, etc.;
The respiratory system is a source of water and heat loss. Inspired atmospheric air is humidified and warmed in the airways before reaching the alveoli.

blocks.text: Between the trachea and the alveolar sacs, the airways divide on average 23 times:
-convection zone: conduction of inspired or expired gas mixtures;
-transition zone: partially honeycombed and therefore allows exchanges;

blocks.text: The alveoli, numbering approximately 300 million in adults, are the site of gas exchange with the blood.

pages.title: Chapter 1: Introduction to respiratory physiology IV-Organization of the respiratory system:

blocks.text: The alveolar-capillary wall is made up of four elements from the inside of the alveolus towards the capillaries:
a fluid film which contains the lung's surface-active substance or surfactant;
-connective tissue rich in elastic fibers and collagen fibers;
the capillary endothelium: the surface area of ​​the alveoli in contact with the capillaries is approximately 70m² and the thickness of this wall is approximately 0.3 to 0.5µm.
